I've drafted a PR (#44636) to refactor LinearMap.trace to work for finite projective modules. The new definition uses the dual-tensor equivalence introduced in #40297 and #41479 to transfer the natrual contraction map from M* ⊗ M to R. There are several discussions (see e.g. Zulip - Determinant under restriction of scalars or PR #40297 review comment) already mentioning this as a possible enhancement, so I think it might be good to just step up and make it a PR.

As @Kevin Buzzard pointed out here, junk values sometimes are not desirable. Previously, LinearMap.trace chooses a finite basis if one exists, and returns junk value otherwise. For projective modules that are not free, this might cause confusion. Instead, in our approach [Module.Finite R M] [Module.Projective R M] is explicitly required. As a consequence, we rewrite several downstream results with their corresponding rank-one proofs, as they generalize the original statement to the finite projective case naturally, and could be consider more canonical.

The PR is now almost ready for review, but as it is somewhat a huge change (400+ LOC changes across 30 files), I would like to get some feedback on whether this is done right, whether something is missing, and whether it should be split into smaller PRs. Appreciate your suggestions!

  • Note that Algebra.intTrace and LinearMap.det are not touched by this PR. I presume they can be addressed in a follow-up PR.
  • I use Codex to help identify affected downstream lemmas and suggest changes. They are manually reviewed and edited afterwards.
I've been waiting for this for a while! Nice!

It's new to me that the trace can be defined on an endomorphism of a finitely generated projective module. My naive idea is that choose a finitely generated N such that M × N is a finitely generated free R-module, now f : M → M extends to (f, 0) : M × N → M × N which is an endomorphism of a finitely generated free module, and whose trace is defined in the usual way. Is this the trace of f? I think this is well-defined and is independent of the choice of N. Similarly one can define the determinant of f by considering (f, 1).
Mathematically the best way is to work locally, as projective is equivalent to locally free.

I think the idea of defining the trace in this way follows from a basic linear algebra observation: taking trace of a rank-one endomorphism f.smulRight mis exactly f m, and you just linearly extend it, as every endomorphism can be decomposed into a sum of rank-one endomorphisms. In fancy language this is the contraction M∗⊗MM^* \otimes MM∗⊗M transferred to End⁡(M)\operatorname{End}(M)End(M) via the dual-tensor equivalence. The ability of "decomposing an endomorphism into rank-one endomorphisms" is exactly encoded into projectivity of MMM, as one of its equivalent condition is the existence of a projective basis.

I think there are two level of "independence" that is worth noting here. In our context, a basic level is to assume freeness, choose a basis arbitrarily, define the trace based on it and show its value does not depend on the choice. Likewise for other formulations that require a choice of some non-canonical structure in prior. But a more canonical idea is to just refrain from choosing a basis at the beginning. Projectivity and its characterization via dual-tensor equivalence seem to be the right formulation that achieves this higher level of independence.
